claims.assertion: Yes — covered service providers must make an accessibility information document available to the public in accessible written and oral formats. TTJA says its purpose is similar to the public-sector accessibility statement, although the Act sets no required structure.

sources.section: Frequently Asked Questions → Overview of the Products and Services Accessibility Act → What must the information document describing the conformity of the service with accessibility requirements contain?
sources.evidence:
Subsection 2 of § 11 of the Products and Services Accessibility Act requires service providers to prepare an information document explaining the conformity of the service with accessibility requirements. This document must be made available to the public in written and oral accessible format and retained throughout the entire period during which the service is provided.

The information document is similar to the accessibility statement currently mandatory in the public sector. Its purpose is to inform users, provide explanations and offer a practical and user-friendly solution for accessibility-related concerns. The statement must include information about the owner of the relevant website and/or application and explain how the service complies with accessibility requirements.

The Products and Services Accessibility Act does not prescribe a specific structure for the information document, meaning that service providers may determine its format at their own discretion. Service providers may consult public sector accessibility statement templates and guidance materials; however, the information document itself must comply with the requirements established by the Products and Services Accessibility Act.

In addition, it is recommended to continue the common practice widely used in Estonia, where a clearly distinguishable link to the accessibility statement is placed in the header or footer of every webpage. The statement may be prepared on the basis of an accessibility assessment carried out either internally or by a partner organisation (such as a developer or an accessibility assessment provider).

claims.review_note: Existing No changed to Yes because the competent authority now explicitly confirms a public information document comparable in purpose to an accessibility statement. Oral availability does not mean a required audio recording. Isolated Estonian-language review on 2026-09-24 by /root/estonian_language (fork_turns=none) found this wording Supported. Maintainer clarification on 2026-09-24: Erik supplied the full English FAQ passage reproduced verbatim in sources[0].evidence and accepted Yes because TTJA explicitly compares the public document with the public-sector statement and recommends the established practice. Yes is retained on that basis. A dedicated webpage or header/footer link is not expressly mandatory: the link is recommended and the document format is discretionary. The information_mode is public_other to preserve that distinction; this is not a claim that WAD applies to private-sector services. No translation or new public-table wording is introduced by this documentation update.

claims.assertion: The Consumer Protection and Technical Regulatory Authority (TTJA) supervises conformity with Estonia’s Products and Services Accessibility Act for covered products and services.

sources.evidence: The Act assigns state supervision of its product and service requirements to TTJA.
TTJA publishes sector guidance for e-commerce, electronic communications, e-books, financial services, passenger transport and audiovisual-access services.

claims.review_note: The official law supports a single competent authority across the Act’s covered sectors. Isolated language review found the mapping Supported.
